chapter.name: Elections
chapter.blurb: Why elections matter, electoral systems, election laws and delimitation, the Election Commission, political parties and defection, and challenges to free and fair elections.

concepts.name: Why elections matter: direct and indirect elections
concepts.description: Laxmikanth: direct and indirect elections (Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, Councils, President), the duration of the Houses, voting behaviour and psephology.
concepts.idea: Regular elections, direct for the popular Houses and indirect for the Rajya Sabha, Councils and President, are the means by which the Constitution makes free and fair elections part of its basic structure.
concepts.rule: The Lok Sabha and state assemblies are directly elected on adult franchise (18 since the 61st Amendment, 1988). Rajya Sabha members of the states are elected by the elected assembly members, a Legislative Council is five-sixths indirectly elected and one-sixth nominated, and the President is chosen by an electoral college of elected members of Parliament, the state assemblies and the assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry. The Lok Sabha runs for five years, the Rajya Sabha is a continuing chamber. Psephology is the scientific study of voting behaviour; its determinants include caste, religion, language, region, personality, money and the performance of the ruling party. Free and fair elections figure among the elements of the basic structure.
concepts.example: A President is chosen by an electoral college of elected legislators, while a Lok Sabha member is chosen directly by the voters of a constituency (Ch.18 p.276, Ch.23 p.328).

questions.q: Which one of the following bodies or offices is NOT filled, wholly or in part, through votes cast by the elected members of the state legislative assemblies?
questions.a: The Lok Sabha (members from the states)
o: The Lok Sabha (members from the states)
The Rajya Sabha (members from the states)
The office of the President of India
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.23 Parliament, p.328: the Lok Sabha members from the states are directly elected by the people on adult franchise; Rajya Sabha members from the states are elected by the elected members of the state assemblies. Ch.33 State Legislature, p.482: one-third of a Council is elected by the assembly members. Ch.18 President, p.276: elected assembly members form part of the electoral college.
w: Rejected: assembly members elect the states' Rajya Sabha representatives (p.328).
Rejected: one-third of a Council is elected by members of the assembly (p.482).
Rejected: elected assembly members vote in the presidential electoral college (p.276).

questions.q: According to Laxmikanth, the several factors that determine voting behaviour in India can be divided into two broad categories, namely
o: personal and psychological factors and institutional factors
local factors and national factors, depending on the level of the election
economic factors and cultural and religious factors
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.84 Voting Behaviour, p.836: because Indian society is highly diversified, the determinants of voting behaviour are divided into socio-economic factors and political factors.
w: Rejected: the book does not use a personal/institutional division (p.836).
Rejected: the book does not divide the factors by the level of the election (p.836).
Rejected: religion is only one of the socio-economic factors; the two categories are different (p.836).

questions.q: The makers of the Constitution did not leave the election of the President to the members of the two Houses of Parliament alone, mainly because
questions.a: a Parliament dominated by one party would invariably have chosen a candidate of that party, who could not represent the states
o: a Parliament dominated by one party would invariably have chosen a candidate of that party, who could not represent the states
the nominated members of Parliament would then have been excluded from voting, which was thought unfair to them
the Rajya Sabha is itself indirectly elected and so cannot take part in choosing the head of state
the Constitution requires the head of state to be chosen by the people of India in a direct vote
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.18 President, p.278: the framers rejected election by Parliament alone because a Parliament dominated by one party would have chosen a candidate from that party, and such a President could not represent the states; the present system makes the President a representative of the Union and the states equally.
w: Rejected: the exclusion of nominated members is a feature of the existing college, not the stated reason (p.276, 278).
Rejected: Rajya Sabha members do vote in the electoral college; this is not the reason given (p.276, 278).
Rejected: the book says direct election was NOT chosen, being costly and anomalous for a nominal head (p.278).

questions.q: The constitutional provision that no person shall be ineligible for inclusion in an electoral roll, or claim to be included in a special electoral roll, on grounds only of religion, race, caste or sex is contained in Article
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections, p.819 (Table 81.2): Article 325 bars ineligibility for, or a claim to a special roll on, grounds of religion, race, caste or sex. Article 324 vests superintendence in the Election Commission, 326 provides adult suffrage and 327 gives Parliament the power to make election law.
w: Rejected: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission (p.819).
Rejected: Article 326 provides for adult suffrage for the Lok Sabha and assemblies (p.819).
Rejected: Article 327 is the power of Parliament to legislate on elections (p.819).

questions.q: Psephology, a term popularised by American political scientists and sociologists, is the branch of political science that deals with
questions.a: the scientific study of voting behaviour
o: the scientific study of voting behaviour
the legal rules governing the conduct of elections
the classification of political parties by ideology
the comparison of electoral systems of different countries
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.84 Voting Behaviour, p.835: psephology deals with the scientific study of voting behaviour (the study of how and why people vote as they do).
w: Rejected: election law belongs to the Representation of the People Acts (Ch.82), not psephology.
Rejected: classifying parties by ideology is the left-centre-right scheme of Ch.79, not psephology.
Rejected: comparing electoral systems is not what the book says psephology is.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election process described by Laxmikanth:

1. The official campaign lasts at least two weeks from the drawing up of the list of nominated candidates.
2. Polling is normally held on a number of different days in different constituencies, to enable the security forces and those monitoring the election to keep law and order.
3. Ballot papers are printed with the symbols allotted to the candidates but without their names.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.815. Statement 2 is correct: p.816. Statement 3 is incorrect: ballot papers are printed with the names of the candidates, in languages set by the Election Commission, and the symbols allotted to them, p.816 (Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.815
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.815
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.815

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the manner of election of a State Legislative Council:

1. One-third of the members are elected by the members of local bodies in the state such as municipalities and district boards.
2. One-twelfth of the members are elected by teachers of three years' standing, not lower in standard than secondary school.
3. One-third of the members are elected by the members of the legislative assembly from among persons who are not members of the assembly.
4. The remaining members, one-sixth of the total, are nominated by the Governor from persons with special knowledge or practical experience of literature, science, art, cooperative movement and social service.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.482. Statement 2 is correct: p.482. Statement 3 is correct: the assembly elects them from persons who are not its members, p.482. Statement 4 is correct: p.482-483 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature); thus five-sixths are indirectly elected and one-sixth nominated.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.482
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.482
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.482

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the determinants of voting behaviour, as described by Laxmikanth:

1. Despite India being a secular nation, no political party ignores the influence of religion in electoral politics.
2. The language factor has ceased to matter since the reorganisation of states on a linguistic basis.
3. Regional parties appeal to the electorate on the ground of regional identities and regional sentiments.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.836. Statement 2 is incorrect: the reorganisation of states on a language basis, and the rise of the DMK and the TDP, are cited as showing the significance of the language factor, p.836. Statement 3 is correct: p.836 (Laxmikanth Ch.84 Voting Behaviour).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.836
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.836
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.836

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the elections of the President and the Vice-President:

1. The electoral college for the Vice-President includes the nominated members of Parliament, whereas that for the President includes only elected members.
2. The election can be challenged before the Supreme Court on the ground that the electoral college was incomplete because of vacancies among its members.
3. A candidate must secure a fixed quota, obtained by dividing the total valid votes by the number of candidates to be elected plus one and adding one to the quotient.
4. If no candidate reaches the quota on first preferences, the candidate with the fewest first-preference votes is eliminated and his second-preference votes are transferred.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Vice-President's college consists of both elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament, Ch.19 Vice-President p.301. Statement 2 is incorrect: all disputes are decided by the Supreme Court, but the election cannot be challenged on the ground that the electoral college was incomplete, p.278. Statement 3 is correct: p.277. Statement 4 is correct: p.277 (Laxmikanth Ch.18 President).
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.278
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.278
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.278

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the duration of the two Houses of Parliament:

1. The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years from the date of its first meeting after the general elections.
2. The Rajya Sabha is dissolved after every six years and a fresh House is elected.
3. During a national emergency the term of the Lok Sabha can be extended by a law of Parliament for one year at a time.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.331. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Rajya Sabha is a continuing chamber, not subject to dissolution; one-third retire every second year, p.331. Statement 3 is correct: p.331 (Laxmikanth Ch.23 Parliament); the extension cannot run beyond six months after the emergency ceases.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.331
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.331
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.331

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about voting behaviour in India, as described by Laxmikanth:

1. In a wave election, local calculations and caste coalitions decide the outcome of the contest.
2. Money can influence the decisions of voters in normal circumstances but not in a wave election.
3. Anti-incumbency means the personal and emotional association of voters with a political party.
4. The defeat of the Congress in 1977 and of the Janata Party in 1980 is cited to illustrate the effect of the performance of the ruling party.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: a wave election rests on issues that transcend local calculations and coalitions, p.837. Statement 2 is correct: p.836. Statement 3 is incorrect: anti-incumbency is dissatisfaction with the performance of the ruling party; emotional association is party identification, p.837. Statement 4 is correct: p.837 (Laxmikanth Ch.84 Voting Behaviour).
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.837
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.837
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.837

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about free and fair elections and the basic structure of the Constitution:

1. In Kuldip Nayar (2006), the Supreme Court struck down the dispensing of the requirement that a Rajya Sabha candidate be an elector in the state concerned.
2. Free and fair elections are listed among the elements of the basic structure of the Constitution.
3. In the Indira Nehru Gandhi case (1975), the Court invalidated a provision of the 39th Amendment that kept election disputes involving the Prime Minister and the Speaker outside the jurisdiction of all courts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: in 2006 the Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of dispensing with the state-elector requirement, Ch.23 p.332. Statement 2 is correct: item 14 of the list, Ch.12 Basic Structure p.200. Statement 3 is correct: Ch.12 p.198-199, and the table on p.201 records free and fair elections as implied in democracy.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.332
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.332
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.332

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the electoral system under the Constitution:

1. There is to be only one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency for elections to Parliament and the state legislatures.
2. Article 326 bases the elections to the Rajya Sabha and the state legislative councils, as well as to the Lok Sabha, on adult suffrage.
3. The Constitution has abolished the system of communal representation and separate electorates.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.813. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 326 bases elections to the House of the People and the state Legislative Assemblies on adult suffrage, p.813, 819. Statement 3 is correct: p.813 (Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.813
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.813
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.813

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the franchise:

1. The 61st Amendment Act (1988) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years for the Lok Sabha as well as the assembly elections.
2. The reduction came into force on 28 March 1989.
3. A citizen who is 18 years old is entitled to vote even if disqualified on the ground of non-residence, unsound mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Ch.83 p.826 and Ch.81 p.813. Statement 2 is correct: Ch.81 footnote 2 on p.819-820. Statement 3 is incorrect: the entitlement holds only if the person is not disqualified under the Constitution or a law on grounds of non-residence, unsound mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice, p.813.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.826
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.826
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.826

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the time of elections:

1. Elections for the Lok Sabha and every state Legislative Assembly have to take place every five years, unless called earlier.
2. The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha and call a general election before five years are up if the Government can no longer command the confidence of the Lok Sabha and no alternative government is available.
3. After a general election the Governor convenes the Lok Sabha to hold its sessions.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.815. Statement 2 is correct: p.815. Statement 3 is incorrect: the President convenes the Lok Sabha, and the Governors the state Assemblies, p.817 (Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections). So exactly two are correct.
w: Miscount: statements 1 and 2 are correct, so one is too few.
Miscount: statement 3 is incorrect, so not all three.
Miscount: statements 1 and 2 are correct, so 'none' is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Rajya Sabha:

1. Every state has the same number of Rajya Sabha representatives, as every state has in the United States Senate.
2. The American Senate has no nominated members.
3. The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from among persons with special knowledge or practical experience in sports and public administration.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Rajya Sabha seats are allotted to states on the basis of population (Uttar Pradesh 31, Tripura 1), p.328. Statement 2 is correct: p.328. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 12 are chosen for art, literature, science and social service, p.328 (Laxmikanth Ch.23 Parliament). So exactly one is correct.
w: Miscount: statement 2 is correct, so 'only two' overcounts.
Miscount: statements 1 and 3 are incorrect.
Miscount: statement 2 is correct, so 'none' undercounts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about voting behaviour:

1. A wave election is one in which a clear tendency develops among the electorate, in a single direction, in favour of a national party or its leader.
2. Voting behaviour is also known as electoral behaviour.
3. According to Paul Brass, quoted by Laxmikanth, caste solidarity remains by far the most important factor in voting behaviour at the local level in the countryside.
4. The study of voting behaviour helps in examining the internalisation of democracy as a value among the elite as well as the masses.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.837. Statement 2 is correct: p.835. Statement 3 is correct: p.836. Statement 4 is correct: p.835 (Laxmikanth Ch.84 Voting Behaviour). So all four are correct.
w: Miscount: all four statements are on the pages, so three is too few.
Miscount: all four are correct, so two is too few.
Miscount: all four are correct, so one is too few.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Constitution has abolished the system of communal representation and separate electorates.
Statement-II: The system of communal representation and separate electorates had led to the partition of the country.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections, p.813: the Constitution has abolished the system of communal representation and separate electorates 'which led to the partition of the country'. Statement-I is correct and the page itself gives Statement-II as the reason for the abolition.
w: Rejected: the page links the abolition to the role of separate electorates in the Partition (p.813).
Rejected: Statement-II is correct (p.813).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.813).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The members of a State Legislative Council are directly elected by the people on the basis of universal adult franchise.
Statement-II: Five-sixths of the members of a legislative council are indirectly elected and one-sixth are nominated by the Governor.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature, p.481-483: the legislative assembly is directly elected on adult franchise, whereas the members of the council are indirectly elected. Statement-I is therefore incorrect. Statement-II is correct: 5/6 are indirectly elected and 1/6 nominated by the Governor (p.483).
w: Rejected: Statement-II is correct, one-sixth are nominated (p.483).
Rejected: Statement-I is incorrect, since council members are indirectly elected (p.482).
Rejected: Statement-I is incorrect, so no explanation can hold (p.482).

questions.q:
Match the body or office in List-I with the manner of its election in List-II.

List-I (Body or office)
A. Lok Sabha members from the states
B. Rajya Sabha members from the states
C. President of India
D. Graduates' share of a State Legislative Council

List-II (Manner of election)
1. Elected by the elected members of the state assemblies by the single transferable vote
2. Elected by graduates of three years' standing residing in the state
3. Elected by an electoral college that includes the elected members of the Delhi and Puducherry assemblies
4. Elected directly by the people from territorial constituencies on adult franchise
questions.e: Ch.23 Parliament p.328: Lok Sabha members are directly elected; Rajya Sabha members of the states are elected by the elected assembly members by the single transferable vote. Ch.18 President p.276: electoral college including Delhi and Puducherry. Ch.33 State Legislature p.482: 1/12 of the Council is elected by graduates of three years' standing.
w: A and B are interchanged: the Lok Sabha is directly elected, the Rajya Sabha indirectly.
B and C are interchanged: the Rajya Sabha is chosen by assembly members, the President by the wider college.
C and D are interchanged: the President is not elected by graduates.

concepts.name: Electoral systems: FPTP and proportional representation
concepts.description: Laxmikanth: first-past-the-post, proportional representation by the single transferable vote, and the bicameral state legislatures.
concepts.idea: The Constitution uses first-past-the-post for the Lok Sabha and assemblies and proportional representation by the single transferable vote for the Rajya Sabha, Councils, President and Vice-President.
concepts.rule: In single-member constituencies the candidate with the largest number of votes wins. Proportional representation was not adopted for the Lok Sabha because of its complexity for voters and its tendency to multiply parties. Six states have a Legislative Council, which Parliament can create or abolish by ordinary law under Article 169 after an assembly resolution by special majority; its strength is at most one-third of the assembly and at least 40.
concepts.example: A candidate with 31 per cent of the votes wins a Lok Sabha seat in a four-cornered contest under first-past-the-post (Ch.81 p.817).

questions.q: In a Lok Sabha constituency four candidates polled 31, 27, 23 and 19 per cent of the valid votes. Under the system the Constitution has adopted for Lok Sabha elections, the Returning Officer will declare
questions.a: the candidate with 31 per cent elected, although most voters voted for others
o: the candidate with 31 per cent elected, although most voters voted for others
no candidate elected, as none has more than half of the votes, and order a fresh poll
the candidate with 31 per cent elected, but only after the votes of the last-placed candidate are transferred to the others
a run-off between the two leading candidates, to be held after the first count
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections, p.817: Lok Sabha elections use the first-past-the-post system; each elector casts one vote and the winner is the candidate who gets the maximum votes. Ch.23 Parliament, p.330: a single-member constituency elects only one representative, and this simple majority system does not represent the whole electorate.
w: Rejected: the Constitution does not require an absolute majority; the largest number of votes wins (p.817).
Rejected: each constituency elects only one representative (p.330).
Rejected: there is no run-off under the first-past-the-post system (p.817).

questions.q: Which one of the following is among the reasons for which the Constitution did not adopt proportional representation for the Lok Sabha?
questions.a: Its tendency to multiply political parties, making it unsuitable to parliamentary government because of instability
o: Its tendency to multiply political parties, making it unsuitable to parliamentary government because of instability
Its failure to protect minorities and small groups, which makes it inferior to the territorial system
The rejection of the system by the Constituent Assembly for every legislature, including the Rajya Sabha
Its inconsistency with federalism, since it gives the states unequal representation in the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.23 Parliament, p.330: the two reasons are the difficulty voters would face in a complicated system given low literacy, and the unsuitability to parliamentary government due to the tendency of the system to multiply parties and cause instability.
w: Rejected: proportional representation helps minorities; the shortcoming is of the territorial system (p.330).
Rejected: some members advocated it and it is used for the Rajya Sabha, councils, President and Vice-President (p.330).
Rejected: not a reason given by the book; Lok Sabha seats follow population (p.329, 330).
tr: defect of FPTP mistaken for reason

questions.q: Under Article 169 of the Constitution, a Legislative Council of a state can be created or abolished by
questions.a: Parliament by an ordinary law, after the assembly passes a resolution by a special majority
o: Parliament by an ordinary law, after the assembly passes a resolution by a special majority
Parliament by an Article 368 amendment, ratified by at least half of the state legislatures
the President by a notification, on the recommendation of the Governor of the state
the state legislature by a law passed by both its Houses by a simple majority
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature, p.480: Parliament can abolish or create a council if the state assembly passes a resolution by a special majority; the Act is not deemed an amendment under Article 368 and is passed like an ordinary law by simple majority.
w: Rejected: the Act is not treated as an Article 368 amendment, so no ratification by states is needed (p.480).
Rejected: the President acts by notification only for the Madhya Pradesh provision, not for Article 169 (p.480).
Rejected: the state legislature can only pass the resolution; Parliament makes the law (p.480).

questions.q: Which one of the following states is NOT among the six states that, according to Laxmikanth, have a bicameral legislature?
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature, p.480: the six bicameral states are Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka. The 7th Amendment (1956) provided for a council in Madhya Pradesh but no Presidential notification has been made, so it continues with one House.
w: Rejected: Karnataka is one of the six bicameral states (p.480).
Rejected: Bihar is one of the six bicameral states (p.480).
Rejected: Telangana is one of the six bicameral states (p.480).

questions.q: The maximum strength of a State Legislative Council is fixed by the Constitution at
questions.a: one-third of the total strength of the legislative assembly of the state
o: one-third of the total strength of the legislative assembly of the state
one-half of the total strength of the legislative assembly of the state
two-thirds of the total strength of the legislative assembly of the state
one-fourth of the total strength of the legislative assembly of the state
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature, p.482: the maximum strength of the council is one-third of the total strength of the assembly and the minimum is 40; the actual strength is fixed by Parliament.
w: Rejected: one-half is not the limit; the cap is one-third (p.482).
Rejected: two-thirds would make the council larger than intended; the cap is one-third (p.482).
Rejected: one-fourth is not the constitutional limit; it is one-third (p.482).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election of members to the Lok Sabha:

1. Every member represents a geographical constituency from which only one representative is elected.
2. The candidate declared elected must secure more than half of the valid votes polled in the constituency.
3. The state legislative assemblies too are elected in single-member constituencies on the first-past-the-post system.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.330. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.330 itself calls this a 'simple majority system' and p.817 says the winner is the candidate who gets the maximum votes, not necessarily more than half. Statement 3 is correct: p.817 (Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections; Ch.23 p.330).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.330
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.330
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.330

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about proportional representation:

1. Under proportional representation all sections of the people get representation in proportion to their numbers.
2. There are two kinds of proportional representation, the single transferable vote system and the list system.
3. India has adopted the list system of proportional representation for the Rajya Sabha and the state legislative councils.
4. India uses the single transferable vote system also in the election of the President and the Vice-President.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.330. Statement 2 is correct: p.330. Statement 3 is incorrect: the first kind, the single transferable vote, is adopted for the Rajya Sabha and the councils, p.330. Statement 4 is correct: p.330 (Laxmikanth Ch.23 Parliament).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.330
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.330
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.330

questions.q:
Consider the following demerits of the system of proportional representation, as listed by Laxmikanth:

1. It increases the significance of the voter and decreases that of the party system.
2. It does not give any scope for organising by-elections.
3. It eliminates intimate contacts between voters and their representatives.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the book says it increases the significance of the party system and decreases that of the voter, p.331. Statement 2 is correct: p.331. Statement 3 is correct: p.331 (Laxmikanth Ch.23 Parliament).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.331
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.331
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.331

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the creation and abolition of Legislative Councils:

1. The assembly's resolution must be passed by a majority of its total membership and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. The Act of Parliament creating or abolishing a council is deemed an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.
3. The Tamil Nadu Legislative Council Act, 2010 created a council that has been functioning in the state since the enactment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.480. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Act is not deemed an amendment for Article 368 and is passed by simple majority, p.480. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 2010 Act was not enforced, because the Assembly passed another resolution in 2011 seeking abolition of the proposed council, p.480-481 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature).
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.480
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.480
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.480

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the second chamber in the states:

1. The Constituent Assembly unanimously supported the idea of a second chamber in the states.
2. The Legislative Council is the upper house, the house of elders, and the Legislative Assembly is the popular house.
3. The Legislative Council is a continuing chamber, one-third of whose members retire on the expiration of every second year.
4. The Legislative Council is dissolved whenever the Legislative Assembly is dissolved.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the idea was criticised in the Constituent Assembly as unrepresentative, delaying and expensive, Ch.33 p.480. Statement 2 is correct: p.480. Statement 3 is correct: p.483. Statement 4 is incorrect: the council is a continuing chamber, not subject to dissolution, p.483 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.480
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.480
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.480

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the system of election followed for different bodies:

1. The Lok Sabha members from the states are elected by the first-past-the-post system.
2. The members of a state legislative assembly are elected by proportional representation by the single transferable vote.
3. The elected members of a state legislative council are chosen by proportional representation by the single transferable vote.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.330, 817. Statement 2 is incorrect: assemblies are elected like the Lok Sabha, in single-member constituencies on first-past-the-post, p.817. Statement 3 is correct: p.483 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.330
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.330
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.330

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of a state legislative assembly:

1. The assembly consists of representatives directly elected by the people on the basis of universal adult franchise.
2. The maximum strength of the assembly is fixed at 600 and the minimum strength at 60.
3. In the case of Mizoram the minimum number of members is fixed at 46.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.481. Statement 2 is incorrect: the maximum strength is 500 (minimum 60), p.481. Statement 3 is incorrect: for Mizoram the minimum is 40, p.481 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.481
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.481
'2 and 3 only' includes statements 2 and 3, which are incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.481

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about State Legislative Councils:

1. The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council was abolished by the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.
2. The Legislative Council of Andhra Pradesh was abolished in 1985 and later revived under the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council Act, 2005.
3. In 2011 the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly passed a resolution seeking the abolition of the proposed Legislative Council.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.480. Statement 2 is correct: p.480-481. Statement 3 is correct: p.481 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature).
w: '2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.480
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.480
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.480

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of a Legislative Council:

1. Though the Constitution fixes the maximum and minimum strength of a council, its actual strength is fixed by Parliament.
2. The scheme of composition of a council laid down in the Constitution is final and Parliament cannot modify or replace it.
3. The size of the council is tied to one-third of the assembly to ensure the predominance of the directly elected House in the legislative affairs of the state.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.482. Statement 2 is incorrect: the scheme is tentative and not final; Parliament is authorised to modify or replace it, p.483. Statement 3 is correct: p.482 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.482
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.482
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.482

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the voting procedure described by Laxmikanth:

1. Voting at the polling station is by secret ballot.
2. On entering the polling station the elector is checked against the electoral roll and indelible ink is applied on the right forefinger.
3. Each polling station is open for at least four hours on the day of the election.
4. Polling stations are usually set up only in police stations and other offices of the district administration.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.816. Statement 2 is incorrect: the ink is applied on the left forefinger, p.816. Statement 3 is incorrect: each polling station is open for at least eight hours, p.816. Statement 4 is incorrect: polling stations are usually set up in public institutions such as schools and community halls, p.816 (Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections). So exactly one is correct.
w: Miscount: only statement 1 is correct, so two overcounts.
Miscount: only statement 1 is correct, so three overcounts.
Miscount: statements 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect, so not all four.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the legislatures of the states:

1. Twenty-two states have a unicameral legislature consisting of the Governor and the legislative assembly.
2. In a state with a bicameral system, the legislature consists of the Governor, the legislative council and the legislative assembly.
3. The legislative council (Vidhan Parishad) is the upper house and the legislative assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is the lower house.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.480. Statement 2 is correct: p.480. Statement 3 is correct: p.480 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature). So all three are correct.
w: Miscount: all three are on p.480, so two is too few.
Miscount: all three are correct, so one is too few.
Miscount: all three are correct, so 'none' is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the legislative assembly of a state:

1. The normal term of a legislative assembly is five years from the date of its first meeting after the general elections.
2. The President is authorised to dissolve a state legislative assembly before the completion of five years.
3. The term of an assembly cannot be extended even during a national emergency.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.483. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is the Governor who may dissolve the assembly at any time, p.483. Statement 3 is incorrect: Parliament may extend the term during a national emergency by law, for one year at a time, p.483 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature). So exactly one is correct.
w: Miscount: statement 1 is correct, so 'none' undercounts.
Miscount: statements 2 and 3 are incorrect, so two overcounts.
Miscount: statements 2 and 3 are incorrect, so three overcounts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Constitution did not adopt proportional representation for the election of members to the Lok Sabha.
Statement-II: Proportional representation tends to multiply political parties, which makes it unsuited to a parliamentary government because of the instability it leads to.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.23 Parliament, p.330: the Constitution has not adopted the system for the Lok Sabha due to two reasons, one being its unsuitability to parliamentary government owing to the tendency to multiply parties and cause instability. Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is a reason the page itself gives.
w: Rejected: the page itself offers Statement-II as a reason for Statement-I (p.330).
Rejected: Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect (p.330).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.330).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Parliament can create a Legislative Council in a state where none exists only if the legislative assembly of that state passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority.
Statement-II: The seats in the Rajya Sabha are allotted to the states on the basis of population.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature, p.480 (Article 169). Statement-II is correct: Ch.23 Parliament, p.328. The allotment of Rajya Sabha seats has no bearing on how a state council is created, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.
w: Rejected: Rajya Sabha seat allotment does not explain the Article 169 procedure.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct, since Rajya Sabha seats vary with population (p.328).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct, since Article 169 needs the assembly's special majority resolution (p.480).

questions.q:
Match the term in List-I with its description in List-II.

List-I (Term)
A. First-past-the-post
B. Proportional representation
C. Single transferable vote
D. Article 169

List-II (Description)
1. The provision for creating or abolishing Legislative Councils in the states
2. The kind of proportional representation adopted for the Rajya Sabha, the councils, the President and the Vice-President
3. All sections of the people get representation in proportion to their numbers
4. The candidate with the largest number of votes in a single-member constituency is elected
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.23 Parliament, p.330-331 and Ch.81 p.817: the first-past-the-post system, proportional representation and the single transferable vote as described; Ch.33 State Legislature, p.480: Article 169 on councils.
w: A and B are interchanged: first-past-the-post elects the top vote-getter; proportional representation gives shares by numbers.
B and C are interchanged: proportional representation is the general principle; the single transferable vote is the kind adopted.
C and D are interchanged: the single transferable vote is a voting method; Article 169 is about councils.

concepts.name: Election laws and delimitation of constituencies
concepts.description: Laxmikanth: the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951, the Delimitation Acts, constitutional bars on courts, and related rules and orders.
concepts.idea: Election law divides between the 1950 Act (seats, delimitation, rolls) and the 1951 Act (conduct, disqualifications, offences, disputes), while delimitation follows each census subject to the freeze.
concepts.rule: The 1950 Act allocates seats and provides for registration of electors; the 1951 Act covers conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, corrupt practices and election petitions. Delimitation is by Parliament's law under Articles 82 and 170, frozen at the 1971 level by the 42nd Amendment and extended up to 2026 by the 84th (the book's wording; Article 82 itself refers to the first census after 2026); the Delimitation Act 2002 used the 2001 census. The validity of delimitation laws cannot be questioned in any court, and election petitions go to the High Courts.
concepts.example: A candidate challenging a Lok Sabha result files an election petition in the High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court (Ch.81 p.813).

questions.q: The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 declares that
questions.a: certain offices of profit under the Government shall not disqualify their holders from being members of Parliament
o: certain offices of profit under the Government shall not disqualify their holders from being members of Parliament
every office of profit under the Government disqualifies its holder from membership of Parliament without exception
a member of Parliament convicted of an offence and sentenced to two years' imprisonment is disqualified
a member who votes contrary to the direction of the party is disqualified from membership of the House
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.82 Election Laws, p.823: the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 declares that certain offices of profit under the Government shall not disqualify the holders for being chosen as, or for being, members of Parliament. Ch.23 p.332 notes that office of profit disqualifies except a minister or any office exempted by Parliament.
w: Rejected: the Act exists precisely to exempt certain offices (p.823).
Rejected: conviction-based disqualification is in the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (Ch.23 p.332), not this Act.
Rejected: defection disqualification is under the Tenth Schedule (Ch.86), not this Act.

questions.q: The authority by which, and the manner in which, seats in the Lok Sabha are readjusted among the states after each census and each state is divided into territorial constituencies is determined by
questions.a: Parliament, by law, as provided in Articles 82 and 170
o: Parliament, by law, as provided in Articles 82 and 170
the Election Commission, by its own orders under Article 324
the Delimitation Commission, constituted by the President without any law of Parliament
the Council of States, by a resolution passed with a special majority
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.82 Election Laws, p.823: Articles 82 and 170 provide for readjustment and division of each state into territorial constituencies by such authority and in such manner as Parliament may by law determine. Ch.23 Parliament, p.329 adds that Parliament has enacted the Delimitation Commission Acts in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002.
w: Rejected: the Election Commission supervises elections; the readjustment authority is set by Parliament's law (p.823).
Rejected: the Commission is created under Parliament's Delimitation Acts, not without a law (p.329, 823).
Rejected: the Rajya Sabha cannot determine this by a resolution; Parliament does so by law (p.823).

questions.q: The Constitution declares that the validity of any law, or of orders of the Delimitation Commission, relating to which one of the following cannot be questioned in any court?
questions.a: The delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies
o: The delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies
The qualifications and disqualifications required of a person for registration as an elector in a constituency
The disqualification of a member of a legislature on the ground of defection under the Tenth Schedule
The registration of political parties by the Election Commission for the purposes of elections
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections, p.813: the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats cannot be questioned in any court, so the orders of the Delimitation Commission become final. Defection decisions are subject to judicial review (Ch.86 p.845).
w: Rejected: the bar is on delimitation laws; electoral qualifications are not given this protection in the text (p.813).
Rejected: the Supreme Court held in Kihoto Hollohan that such decisions are subject to judicial review (Ch.86 p.845).
Rejected: no such constitutional bar attaches to registration of parties (Ch.82 p.822).

questions.q: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Orders (Amendment) Act, 1976 provides for
questions.a: the inclusion in, and the exclusion from, the lists of scheduled castes and scheduled tribes of certain castes and tribes, for readjusting representation
o: the inclusion in, and the exclusion from, the lists of scheduled castes and scheduled tribes of certain castes and tribes, for readjusting representation
the extension of the reservation of seats for scheduled castes and tribes in the Lok Sabha and assemblies by a further ten years
the constitution of a Delimitation Commission to redraw the reserved constituencies on the 1971 census
the grant of separate electorates to scheduled caste and tribe voters in the reserved constituencies
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.82 Election Laws, p.823: the Act provides for the inclusion in, and exclusion from, the lists of SCs and STs of certain castes and tribes, for the readjustment of representation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies.
w: Rejected: the extensions of reservation were made by constitutional amendments (Ch.23 p.330).
Rejected: the Delimitation Acts, not this Act, set up Commissions (p.823-824).
Rejected: there is no separate electorate for reserved seats (Ch.23 p.330).

questions.q: In L. Chandra Kumar vs Union of India (1997), the Supreme Court declared unconstitutional the provision of Article 323B that
questions.a: excluded the jurisdiction of all courts, except the special leave appeal jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, in election disputes
o: excluded the jurisdiction of all courts, except the special leave appeal jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, in election disputes
empowered the appropriate legislature, Parliament or a state legislature, to establish a tribunal for the adjudication of election disputes
barred the courts from questioning the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or allotment of seats
gave the Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction in election petitions arising from the High Courts
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections, p.814 and footnote 3 on p.819: Article 323B also excluded the jurisdiction of all courts (except special leave appeals to the Supreme Court) in election disputes; clause 3(d) was declared unconstitutional in L. Chandra Kumar (1997), so an appeal from any tribunal would lie to the high court.
w: Rejected: the power to establish a tribunal was left in place; only the exclusion of courts was struck down (p.814).
Rejected: the bar on questioning delimitation laws is Article 329, not Article 323B (p.813).
Rejected: Supreme Court appeals in election petitions are not what was struck down (p.813, 814).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Articles relating to elections in Part XV of the Constitution:

1. Article 327 gives Parliament the power to make provision with respect to elections to legislatures.
2. Article 328 gives Parliament the power to make provision with respect to elections to the legislature of a state.
3. Article 329 bars interference by courts in electoral matters.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 81.2, p.819. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 328 is the power of the Legislature of a state to make provision with respect to elections to that Legislature, p.819. Statement 3 is correct: p.819 (Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.819
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.819
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.819

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Representation of the People Act, 1950:

1. It provides for the actual conduct of elections, including the nomination of candidates, the poll and the counting of votes.
2. It provides for the registration of electors and the qualifications and disqualifications for such registration.
3. It provides for election officers such as the chief electoral officers, district election officers and electoral registration officers.
4. It lays down the procedure for presenting election petitions to the High Court.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the conduct of elections is provided by the Act of 1951, p.821-822. Statement 2 is correct: p.821. Statement 3 is correct: p.821. Statement 4 is incorrect: presentation and trial of election petitions are in the Act of 1951, p.822 (Laxmikanth Ch.82 Election Laws).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.821
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.821
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.821

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Delimitation Act, 2002:

1. It was enacted to set up a Delimitation Commission to effect delimitation on the basis of the 2001 census.
2. The previous delimitation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies was based on the 1971 census.
3. It increased the number of Lok Sabha seats allotted to each state in proportion to the population shown by the 2001 census.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.823. Statement 2 is correct: p.823. Statement 3 is incorrect: delimitation on the basis of the 2001 census was to be done without altering the number of seats allotted to each state, Ch.23 Parliament p.329.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.823
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.823
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.823

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution and the Representation of the People Act, 1950:

1. Articles 81 and 170 lay down the maximum number of seats in Parliament and the assemblies and certain principles for allocation, but leave the actual allocation of seats to be provided by law.
2. Article 171 lays down the maximum and minimum number of seats in a Legislative Council and the methods of filling them, but leaves the actual number to be filled by each method to law.
3. The Act of 1950 conferred on the Election Commission the power to delimit the constituencies, after consultation with the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.821. Statement 2 is correct: p.821. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Act conferred on the President the power to delimit constituencies after consultation with the Election Commission, p.821 (Laxmikanth Ch.82 Election Laws).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.821
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.821
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.821

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional provisions on election law:

1. Parliament may make provision on all matters relating to elections to Parliament and the state legislatures, including the preparation of electoral rolls and delimitation of constituencies.
2. A law made by a state legislature on elections to that legislature prevails over a parliamentary law on the same matter.
3. Election petitions can be presented to and tried by any civil court of the district concerned.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.813. Statement 2 is incorrect: state legislatures can only supplement the parliamentary law and cannot override it, p.813. Statement 3 is incorrect: election petitions are triable by the high courts alone, p.813 (Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections).
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.813
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.813
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.813

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rules and orders relating to elections:

1. The Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 provides for the specification, reservation, choice and allotment of symbols and the recognition of political parties.
2. The Registration of Political Parties (Furnishing of Additional Particulars) Order, 1992 provides for additional particulars to be furnished by bodies seeking registration as political parties with the Election Commission.
3. The Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 provide for the specification and allotment of election symbols.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.824. Statement 2 is correct: p.824. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 provide for the preparation and publication of electoral rolls, p.823 (Laxmikanth Ch.82 Election Laws).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.824
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.824
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.824

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about election petitions, as described by Laxmikanth:

1. Any elector or candidate can file an election petition if he or she thinks there has been malpractice during the election.
2. An election petition is an ordinary civil suit between two parties and does not involve the rest of the constituency.
3. If an election petition is upheld, it can even lead to the restaging of the election in that constituency.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.817. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is not an ordinary civil suit but is treated as a contest in which the whole constituency is involved, p.817. Statement 3 is correct: p.817 (Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.817
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.817
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.817

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the readjustment of state assembly constituencies:

1. The 84th Amendment Act (2001) empowered the government to undertake readjustment and rationalisation of territorial constituencies in a state on the basis of the 1991 census figures.
2. After each census a readjustment is to be made in the total number of seats in the assembly of each state and in the division of each state into territorial constituencies.
3. The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) froze the total number of seats in the assembly of each state, and the division into constituencies, till the year 2000 at the 1971 level.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.482. Statement 2 is correct: p.481. Statement 3 is correct: p.482 (Laxmikanth Ch.33 State Legislature).
w: '1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.482
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.482
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.482

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the adjudication of election disputes:

1. A tribunal for the adjudication of election disputes has already been established under Article 323B.
2. Article 323B empowers the appropriate legislature, Parliament or a state legislature, to establish such a tribunal.
3. If a tribunal were established, an appeal from its decision would lie to the high court.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: so far no such tribunal has been established, p.814. Statement 2 is correct: p.813. Statement 3 is correct: after L. Chandra Kumar (1997) an appeal from a tribunal's decision lies to the high court, p.814 (Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.814
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.814
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.814

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Representation of the People Act, 1951:

1. It provides for the registration of political parties.
2. It provides for the free supply of certain material to candidates of recognised political parties.
3. It bars the jurisdiction of civil courts in certain matters.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.822. Statement 2 is correct: p.822. Statement 3 is correct: p.823 (Laxmikanth Ch.82 Election Laws). So all three are correct.
w: Miscount: all three items are in the Act's list, so two is too few.
Miscount: all three are correct, so one is too few.
Miscount: all three are correct, so 'none' is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 regulates certain matters relating to or connected with the elections to the offices of the President and the Vice-President.
2. The Government of Union Territories Act, 1963 and the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991 are listed among the other Acts relating to elections.
3. The 87th Amendment Act (2003) increased the number of Lok Sabha seats allotted to each state.
4. The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Orders (Amendment) Act, 1976 provides for the inclusion in, and the exclusion from, the lists of scheduled castes and scheduled tribes of certain castes and tribes.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Ch.82 p.823. Statement 2 is correct: Ch.82 p.823. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 87th Amendment provided for delimitation on the basis of the 2001 census without altering the number of seats allotted to each state, Ch.23 p.329. Statement 4 is correct: Ch.82 p.823. So exactly three are correct.
w: Miscount: statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so one is too few.
Miscount: statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so two is too few.
Miscount: statement 3 is incorrect, so not all four.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Rules, 1974 repealed the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961.
2. Article 329A, which made a special provision as to the elections of the Prime Minister and the Speaker, continues in force.
3. The Delimitation Act, 2002 was the first law enacted by Parliament on the delimitation of constituencies.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the 1974 Rules repealed the earlier Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Rules, 1952, Ch.82 p.824 footnote 2. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 329A is marked 'Repealed' in Table 81.2, Ch.81 p.819. Statement 3 is incorrect: earlier Delimitation Acts were enacted in 1952, 1962 and 1972, Ch.82 footnote on p.824. So none is correct.
w: Miscount: all three statements are incorrect, so one is too many.
Miscount: all three statements are incorrect, so two is too many.
Miscount: all three statements are incorrect, so three is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The orders issued by the Delimitation Commission become final and cannot be challenged in any court.
Statement-II: The Constitution declares that the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies cannot be questioned in any court.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.81 Elections, p.813: the Constitution declares that the validity of any law relating to delimitation or the allotment of seats cannot be questioned in any court; consequently the orders of the Delimitation Commission become final and cannot be challenged. Statement-II is the stated basis of Statement-I.
w: Rejected: the page draws the link itself with the word 'consequently' (p.813).
Rejected: Statement-II is correct (p.813).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.813).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Delimitation of constituencies on the basis of the 2001 census was provided for without altering the number of Lok Sabha seats allotted to each state.
Statement-II: The previous delimitation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies was based on the 1971 census.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Laxmikanth Ch.23 Parliament, p.329 (87th Amendment). Statement-II is correct: Ch.82 Election Laws, p.823. The earlier basis of delimitation is not the reason the seat numbers were left unaltered, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.
w: Rejected: the page ties the unaltered seat numbers to the freeze, not to the earlier census base (p.329).
Rejected: Statement-II is correct (p.823).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.329).

questions.q:
Match the law in List-I with its subject in List-II.

List-I (Law)
A. Registration of Electors Rules, 1960
B. Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961
C. Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952
D. Delimitation Act, 2002

List-II (Subject)
1. Facilitating the conduct of free and fair elections to Parliament and the state legislatures
2. Delimitation of constituencies on the basis of the 2001 census
3. Preparation and publication of electoral rolls
4. Matters relating to the elections to the offices of the President and the Vice-President
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.82 Election Laws, p.823: Registration of Electors Rules (rolls), Conduct of Elections Rules (free and fair conduct), the 1952 Act (President and Vice-President) and the Delimitation Act 2002 (2001 census).
w: A and B are interchanged: the 1960 Rules concern rolls; the 1961 Rules concern conduct.
B and C are interchanged: the 1961 Rules concern parliamentary and state elections; the 1952 Act concerns the two offices.
C and D are interchanged: the 1952 Act is about the two offices and the 2002 Act about delimitation.

concepts.name: The Election Commission of India and its functions
concepts.description: Laxmikanth: the constitutional status, composition, independence, powers and election machinery of the Election Commission.
concepts.idea: The Election Commission is a permanent constitutional body under Article 324 whose Chief Election Commissioner has the security of tenure of a Supreme Court judge.
concepts.rule: The Commission supervises elections to Parliament, state legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President, not panchayats and municipalities. It has been a three-member body since 1993, the CEC is removable like a Supreme Court judge while other commissioners are removable on the CEC's recommendation, and in Anoop Baranwal (2023) the Court laid down a selection committee pending a law. Its functions are administrative, advisory and quasi-judicial; at the state level it is assisted by a Chief Electoral Officer.
concepts.example: The Commission announces the schedule, the Model Code of Conduct takes effect at once and observers monitor the poll and the expenditure (Ch.81 pp.814-816).

questions.q: The Election Commission of India established under Article 324 is NOT concerned with the conduct of elections to
questions.a: the panchayats and municipalities in the states
o: the panchayats and municipalities in the states
the office of the Vice-President of India
the legislative assemblies of the states
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.43 Election Commission, p.599: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, the state legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Commission; elections to panchayats and municipalities are conducted by a separate State Election Commission (73rd and 74th Amendment Acts).
w: Rejected: the Commission does conduct the Vice-President's election (p.599).
Rejected: state assembly elections are within its authority (p.599).
Rejected: elections to Parliament are within its authority (p.599).

questions.q: In the Anoop Baranwal case (2023), the Supreme Court directed that the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners be appointed on the recommendation of a committee consisting of
questions.a: the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party) and the Chief Justice of India
o: the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party) and the Chief Justice of India
the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Vice-President of India
the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, without the Leader of the Opposition
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.43 Election Commission, p.600-601: the Court declared that the appointments shall be made on the recommendation of a three-member committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party if there is none) and the Chief Justice of India. The directions were to operate until Parliament makes a law in consonance with Article 324. Currency note (outside the book): Parliament later enacted the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which put a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister in the committee in place of the Chief Justice.
w: Rejected: the Speaker is not a member of the committee the Court prescribed (p.601).
Rejected: the Vice-President is not a member (p.601).
Rejected: the Leader of the Opposition was a member and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha was not (p.601).

questions.q: The Election Commission acts as a court, in its quasi-judicial capacity, for settling disputes relating to
questions.a: the recognition of political parties and the allotment of election symbols to them
o: the recognition of political parties and the allotment of election symbols to them
the validity of the election of a member of Parliament, which it hears before the High Court
the disqualification of a legislator on the ground of defection, subject to the Speaker's approval
the delimitation of constituencies, against whose orders appeal lies to the Commission
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.43 Election Commission, p.601: the Commission acts as a court for settling disputes related to the granting of recognition to political parties and the allotment of election symbols. Election petitions go to the High Courts (Ch.81 p.813), defection cases to the presiding officer (Ch.86 p.845) and delimitation orders cannot be challenged in any court (Ch.81 p.813).
w: Rejected: election petitions are tried by the High Courts alone (Ch.81 p.813).
Rejected: defection cases are decided by the presiding officer (Ch.86 p.845).
Rejected: delimitation orders are final and cannot be challenged in any court (Ch.81 p.813).

questions.q: According to the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991, as described by Laxmikanth, the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners hold office for
questions.a: six years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
o: six years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
five years or until they attain the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
six years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is later
a term of six years fixed by the Constitution itself, without any age limit
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.43 Election Commission, p.600: they hold office for six years or until age 65, whichever is earlier. The Constitution itself has not specified the term of the members of the Commission (p.600). Currency note (outside the book): the 1991 Act was repealed by the 2023 Act, which carries the six-years-or-age-65 rule forward.
w: Rejected: five years and 62 are not the figures in the book (p.600).
Rejected: 'whichever is later' reverses the rule; it is the earlier of the two (p.600).
Rejected: the Constitution has not specified the term of the members (p.600).

questions.q: At the state level, the Election Commission is assisted by an officer who is appointed by the Chief Election Commissioner in consultation with the state government. This officer is the
questions.e: Laxmikanth Ch.43 Election Commission, p.602: at the state level the Commission is assisted by the chief electoral officer, appointed by the CEC in consultation with the state government. Ch.81 p.814 adds that the CEO supervises election work in the state or union territory subject to the Commission's control. The State Election Commission deals with local bodies (p.599).
w: Rejected: the State Election Commissioner conducts panchayat and municipal elections, not the Commission's work in the state (p.599).
Rejected: the Chief Secretary is not the Commission's state officer (p.602).
Rejected: Regional Commissioners are appointed by the President after consulting the Commission (p.599).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Election Commission:

1. It consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and such number of other election commissioners as the President may from time to time fix.
2. It has functioned as a three-member body ever since its inception in 1950.
3. The President may appoint, after consultation with the Election Commission, such regional commissioners as he considers necessary to assist it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.599. Statement 2 is incorrect: it functioned as a single-member body from 1950 till 15 October 1989, p.599-600. Statement 3 is correct: p.599 (Laxmikanth Ch.43 Election Commission).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.599
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.599
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.599

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the history of the Election Commission:

1. From its inception in 1950 till 15 October 1989, the Commission functioned as a single-member body.
2. Two more election commissioners were appointed in 1989 to cope with the increased work after the voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years.
3. The two posts of election commissioners were abolished in January 1990 and the Commission reverted to the earlier position.
4. In October 1993 the President again appointed two more election commissioners, and the Commission has since functioned as a multi-member body.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.599. Statement 2 is correct: p.599 and footnote 2 (61st Amendment). Statement 3 is correct: p.600. Statement 4 is correct: p.600 (Laxmikanth Ch.43 Election Commission).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.599
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.599
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.599

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the independence of the Election Commission:
